For the officer joining this caseload, here is a concise orientation summary:  

**District Concentration**: Cases are concentrated in **فیصل آباد** (Faisalabad: 19 cases) and **لاہور** (Lahore: 18 cases), with significantly fewer cases in other districts (e.g., **راولپنڈی** (Rawalpindi: 10), **اسلام آباد** (Islamabad: 5), and others with 5 or fewer cases) [Document 1].  

**Case Mix**: Current cases (2026) include **39 PPC** (Pakistan Penal Code) cases, **16 Arms Ordinance 1965** cases, and newer categories like **CNSA 1997** (12), **PECA 2016** (9, cybercrime), **Punjab Domestic Violence Act** (4), and **Illegal Dispossession Act 2005** (2). This contrasts with 2024, when PPC and Arms Ordinance 1965 dominated [Document 2].  

**Arrest Rates**: Only **11 of 73 FIRs** record at least one arrest; **62 FIRs** show no arrests (e.g., under investigation, absconding) [Document 3].  

**Reporting Delays**: The average time to report crimes rose sharply from **15.0 minutes in 2024** to **1401.3 minutes (~23.4 hours) in 2026** [Document 4].  

**Weapon Licensing**: Of **32 weapon-register entries**, **30 recovered weapons** had **no licence recorded**, and **2 entries** lacked licence status entirely [Document 5].  

This mix demands focus on domestic violence, cybercrime, and land disputes, alongside traditional PPC and arms offenses, with low arrest rates and delayed reporting requiring proactive investigation.
